rule_description: Follow the Google XYZ formula: Accomplished [X] as measured by [Y], by doing [Z]. Always lead with a strong active verb, provide explicit metrics (percentages, ms latency, throughput), and detail the technical mechanism.
before_example: Worked on backend APIs and made database queries faster.
after_example: Optimized SQL indexing and query execution plans across 12 high-traffic PostgreSQL endpoints, reducing p99 API response latency by 42% (from 320ms to 185ms) under 15k peak RPM.
impact_explanation: Replaces passive task description ('worked on') with quantifiable outcome (42% latency reduction) and concrete technical mechanism (indexing and query plans).

rule_description: Quantify user-facing frontend impact using standardized Core Web Vitals or bundle size metrics.
before_example: Built a React dashboard and improved loading speed.
after_example: Architected dynamic code-splitting and asset lazy-loading for core React dashboard modules, cutting initial JavaScript bundle size by 35% and improving Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) from 3.8s to 1.4s.
impact_explanation: Cites specific performance metrics (bundle size, LCP) and technical solutions (code-splitting, lazy-loading) that recruiters and hiring managers look for.

rule_description: Highlight operational efficiency, cost reductions, and deployment frequency improvements.
before_example: Helped move our servers to Docker and AWS.
after_example: Spearheaded containerization of 8 legacy monolithic services using Docker and automated CI/CD deployment pipelines on AWS ECS, reducing deployment release cycle from 3 days to 15 minutes and slashing cloud infrastructure expenses by $18,000 annually.
impact_explanation: Demonstrates business ROI (cost savings, velocity improvement) alongside infrastructure expertise.

rule_description: Never use weak or passive verbs such as 'Assisted with', 'Responsible for', 'Helped', or 'Participated in'. Use high-impact verbs: 'Architected', 'Engineered', 'Spearheaded', 'Streamlined', 'Overhauled', 'Automated'.
before_example: Responsible for maintaining unit tests and code quality.
after_example: Automated end-to-end integration test suites with PyTest and GitHub Actions across 4 microservices, expanding code coverage from 58% to 91% and eliminating critical release regressions.
impact_explanation: Transforms passive duty statement into proactive engineering leadership with measurable coverage gains.

rule_description: Avoid multi-column tables, text boxes, headers/footers for key contact info, and scanned images. Standard single-column linear layout with standard section headers ('Experience', 'Education', 'Skills', 'Projects') ensures 100% ATS parser accuracy.
before_example: Putting contact info and skills in a 2-column sidebar graphic box with custom icon glyphs.
after_example: Single-column linear hierarchy with standard UTF-8 text headers and clear bullet points.
impact_explanation: Legacy and modern ATS parsers (Workday, Taleo, Greenhouse) frequently drop or scramble text embedded inside complex multi-column floating boxes.
